messages:
ashley: Heads up — between 02:10–02:20 UTC saw controller-manager leader flips + apiserver 502/503s in us-west-2 during the scheduled GPU node provisioning window. Rolling restart of controllers didn't stabilize.
mike: Any logs yet? Do we have a correlation with the GPU provisioning job? Could be CNI or NAT exhaustion.
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: apiserver 5xx spike detected in us-west-2 (02:12). Graph: https://metrics.redwood-internal/graph?panel=apiserver_5xx
karen: Pasting controller-manager excerpts — lots of lease renew failures and etcd timeouts:
```
I0310 02:12:14.123456 1 leaderelection.go:255] failed to renew lease: timed out waiting for the condition
E0310 02:12:14.223456 1 reflector.go:205] k8s.io/...: Failed to watch *v1.Pod: etcdserver: request timed out
```
Also `kubectl get pod -n kube-system -o wide | grep controller-manager` shows multiple restarts.
oliver: I checked network egress metrics — NAT gateway SNAT connection count spiked at the same time. We recently ramped GPU nodepool by +220 nodes overnight.
jason: That matches previous incidents — too many pod IPs -> SNAT port exhaustion -> control plane components that call external APIs (S3 snapshots, image registries) start timing out and that propagates into leader election failures.
mike: Can we confirm ETCD snapshot uploads? If snapshots are hitting cross-region S3, that multiplies connections during rolling snapshots.
karen: ETCD snapshots have multiple failed uploads circa 01:58:
```
upload failed: PutObject S3 "403 Access Denied"
curl https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-etcd-snapshots -> 403
```
We had an IAM role rotation earlier at 01:50 for the snapshot uploader — might be a timing overlap.
jason: Short-term mitigation: throttle the GPU provisioning job (maxParallel -> 10) and stagger snapshot/upload windows. I can push a hotfix to the provisioner.
oliver: Long-term options: move etcd snapshot uploads to a regional bucket to avoid cross-region egress and lower concurrent connections, or add a NAT Gateway autoscaling pattern and SNAT port reuse (e.g., use NAT gateway + EIPs per nodepool). Cost tradeoff: regional snapshots + extra NAT capacity will raise monthly costs.
mike: Also consider tuning control plane timeouts and leader-election lease durations to be a bit more resilient to short network blips. But that just masks the root cause.
ashley: I just scaled down the provisioning rollout to 50% and paused new node launches. Also rolled back the IAM rotation for the snapshot uploader while we validate.
jason: PR up: infra/provisioner#478 — throttles parallel adds and adds jitter. Will deploy to canary now.
karen: After the pause, controller-manager leader flips stopped within ~6m and apiserver 5xx returned to baseline. Still seeing a handful of failed snapshot uploads; ops will retry.
oliver: Cost estimate: moving snapshots regional -> ~+12% storage cost but saves ~20% estimated egress spend and reduces incident risk. NAT autoscaling adds $X/month depending on peak, but reduces ops toil.
mike: Can we add a permanent guardrail: provisioner should query current SNAT usage and backoff when above 80%? Also add a preflight to ensure IAM roles for snapshot uploader are not in rotation windows.
ashley: Agreed. I'll file a follow-up RFC to outline mitigations + cost tradeoffs and assign owners. Monitoring alert rule will be tightened to fire before 5xx spike (apiserver latency + SNAT port usage correlation).
ashley: Monitoring for next 30m. If it reappears we'll escalate to incident. :thumbsup:
